DWL? - Pareto efficiency - State where no one can be made better off without someone else being worse off 4 Review Problem 1e.- 1g. 5 Important Concepts Externalities - Graph (Marginal Social Benefit, Marginal Social Cost) - Deadweight Loss = arrow right (positive) or left (negative) - Added cost/benefit - How does it affect the original curves? - Solutions: - Policy: - Pigouvian Taxes - Private: - Coase Theorem (private bargaining) 6 Review Problem 2. 7 Important Concepts Utility - Utility Function - The relationship between how much utility a consumer could receive from certain quantities of two goods - Budget Constraint - Y = p1q1 + p2q2 - Given Y dollars, I can buy q1 and q2 of my two goods at prices p1 and p2 - Indifference Curve - Graph of the utility function - Represents different bundles of two goods where consumer receives the same amount of utility 8 Important Concepts Utility pt. 2 - To find optimum, we want to find where the slope of the indifference curve equals the slope of the budget constraint - Marginal Rate of Substitution - MU1 / MU2 aka (du/dq1 ) / (du/dq2) - Slope of the indifference curve - Marginal Rate of Transformation - P1 / P2 aka (dq2 / dq1) - Set these equal! - Plug values into budget constraint to find optimal quantities 9 Important Concepts Income/Substitution Effects - Effects of a price increase/decrease - Substitution Effect: - Short-term, change in QD, causes movement along indifference curve - Income Effect: - Long-term, change in QD, causes jump to a new indifference curve - Total Effect: - Sum of substitution and income effects - Price Change > SE > IE > Total Effect > New Optimum 10 Review Problem 3. 11 Important Concepts Deriving Cost Curves (Short-Run) - Given Total Cost curve, TC: - Variable Cost, VC = TC - Constants - Fixed Costs, FC = TC - Variable Cost - Average Total Cost, ATC = TC / Q - Average Variable Cost, AVC = VC / Q - Average Fixed Cost, AFC = FC / Q - Marginal Cost, MC = TC’ (derivative) 12 Important Concepts Deriving Cost Curves (Long-Run) - No fixed costs in the long run!!! - Given Total Cost curve, TC: - LR Variable Cost, LRVC = TC - LR Fixed Costs, LRFC = 0 - LR Average Total Cost, LRATC = TC / Q - LR Average Variable Cost, LRAVC = LRATC - LR Average Fixed Cost, AFC = 0 - LR Marginal Cost, LRMC = TC’ (derivative) 13 Important Concepts Cost Curve Relationships (SR) - Profit-Maximizing Price/Quantity: - WHERE MR = MC - Fundamental relationship in Econ! - Price = MR in perfect competition - Shut-Down Point (short-run concept) - Below minimum of AVC curve - At quantity of 0, firm still suffers sunk costs, so they should at least make some of these back - Must be able to cover their variable costs - OK if curve goes below Q = 0 (negative)! 14 Important Concepts Cost Curve Relationships (LR) - Since no fixed costs, LRAVC = LRATC - Equilibrium Price/Quantity where MR = LRATC = MC - Minimum of LRATC curve, aka break- even point (no profit or loss) - If there is profit/loss, firms will enter/leave the market, driving the market back to equilibrium - Supply Curve: Above minimum of AVC in short run, above minimum of LRATC in long run 15 Practice Problem Question 16 Practice Problem Set 4, Problem 1. Parts f, g. 18 Important Concept Trade - Opening up to trade at a world price below equilibrium is like a price ceiling without deadweight loss - Tariffs simply add on to the world price - i.e. world price of $2 plus a $3 tariff = price of $5 - Know where deadweight loss and government revenue occur with a tariff 19 Last Year’s Exam Questions 20 Problems 8. and 35. 21 Important Concept Aggregate Demand - To find the demand for all consumers in a market, we sum their demand curves - BUT BE CAREFUL - If we are talking about a private good, we sum the demand curves horizontally - Consumers cannot consume the same units (rivalrous) - Summing Q’s - If we are talking about a public good, we sum the demand curves vertically - Consumers can consume the same units (non-rivalrous) - Summing P’s 22 Problem 11. 23 Important Concept Elasticity - The elasticity of a good represents how sensitive it is to changes in either its or another good’s price - Represented by how steep the demand/supply curve is - NOT SLOPE - this is percentage change ratio - If the curve is completely horizontal, the good is perfectly elastic (E = 1), meaning quantity demanded changes greatly with a change in price - If the curve is completely vertical, the good is perfectly inelastic (E = 0), meaning quantity demanded does not change at all with changes in price 24 Problem 17. 25 Important Concept Cross-Price Elasticity and Related Goods - Cross-price elasticity of demand represents the change in quantity demanded of good x as the price of good y changes. - IF NEGATIVE - goods are complements - Price of one goes up, QD for the other goes down - IF POSITIVE - goods are substitutes - Price of one goes up, QD for the other goes up 26 Problem 18. 27 Important Concept Effects of Change In Price (Two Goods) - Two effects (price decrease) - SUBSTITUTION EFFECT - Movement down along current indifference curve - You buy less of the good in the short-term - INCOME EFFECT - Jump to a new, higher indifference curve - You are able to buy more of the good in the long-term - Graph it? 28 Problem 28. 29 Important Concept Economies of Scale - The state achieved when long-run average total cost is decreasing as output is increasing - Essentially when per-unit costs decrease when a firm grows as seen in the question - DISECONOMIES OF SCALE - When per-unit costs increase as a firm grows - CONSTANT RETURNS TO SCALE - When per-unit costs stay the same as a firm grows 30 Problem 30. 31 Important Concept Absolute and Comparative Advantage -
